metadata.methods_description: EEG was recorded from 123 participants (75 female, ages 17-38) using a 32-channel biosignal recording system positioned according to the International 10-20 system, sampled at either 1000 Hz (92 subjects) or 250 Hz (31 subjects). Participants viewed 28 video clips (30-129 seconds duration) designed to target nine emotion categories (anger, disgust, fear, sadness, neutral, amusement, inspiration, joy, tenderness) presented in randomized blocks with arithmetic problems between blocks. After each video, participants rated their emotional response on 12 continuous 0-7 scales.

citation_details.title: A Large Finer-grained Affective Computing EEG Dataset
citation_details.author: Jingjing Chen, Xiaobin Wang, Chen Huang, Xin Hu, Xinke Shen, Dan Zhang
citation_details.abstract: Affective computing based on electroencephalogram (EEG) has gained increasing attention for its objectivity in measuring emotional states. While positive emotions play a crucial role in various real-world applications, such as human-computer interactions, the state-of-the-art EEG datasets have primarily focused on negative emotions, with less consideration given to positive emotions. Meanwhile, these datasets usually have a relatively small sample size, limiting exploration of the important issue of cross-subject affective computing. The proposed Finer-grained Affective Computing EEG Dataset (FACED) aimed to address these issues by recording 32-channel EEG signals from 123 subjects. During the experiment, subjects watched 28 emotion-elicitation video clips covering nine emotion categories (amusement, inspiration, joy, tenderness; anger, fear, disgust, sadness, and neutral emotion), providing a fine-grained and balanced categorization on both the positive and negative sides of emotion.

citation_details.author: Yuan Hu, Chenhan Xu, Lin Bo, Wei-Bin Yang, Yuan Yan Tang
citation_details.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has ushered in a new era of medical multimodal large language models (MLLMs), which integrate diverse data modalities such as text, imaging, physiological signals, and genomics to enhance clinical decision-making. This systematic review explores the core methodologies and applied research frontiers of medical MLLMs, focusing on their architecture, training methods, evaluation techniques, and applications. We highlight the transformative potential of MLLMs in achieving cross-modal semantic alignment, medical knowledge integration, and robust clinical reasoning. Despite their promise, challenges such as data heterogeneity, hallucination, and computational efficiency persist. By reviewing state-of-the-art solutions and future directions, this paper provides a comprehensive technical guide for developing reliable and interpretable medical MLLMs, ultimately aiming to bridge the gap between AI and clinical practice.

citation_details.abstract: EEG-based neural decoding models often fail to generalize across acquisition sites due to structured, site-dependent biases implicitly exploited during training. We construct a standardized multi-site EEG benchmark for Major Depressive Disorder and introduce CRCC, a two-stage training paradigm combining encoder-decoder pretraining with joint fine-tuning via cross-subject/site contrastive learning and site-adversarial optimization. CRCC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines and achieves a 10.7 percentage-point improvement in balanced accuracy under strict zero-shot site transfer, demonstrating robust generalization to unseen environments.

citation_details.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG)-based emotion recognition is challenged by the high dimensionality across time samples, epochs, and channels. From this optimized representation, 49 multidomain features were extracted and classified using an ensemble of the hybrid models. AFFEET-R achieved an accuracy of 88.89 %, demonstrating excellent performance, interpretability, and efficiency for real-time EEG-based affective computing.
